name: Anaconda
description: Anaconda, widely known in home games as 'Pass the Trash,' is a high-action poker variant characterized by multiple passing rounds and a dramatic 'rollout' showdown. Unlike traditional poker, players actively sabotage their opponents during the passing phases, making it a game of social manipulation and tactical hand-building.

overview.description: Anaconda, widely known in home games as 'Pass the Trash,' is a high-action poker variant characterized by multiple passing rounds and a dramatic 'rollout' showdown. Unlike traditional poker, players actively sabotage their opponents during the passing phases, making it a game of social manipulation and tactical hand-building.

history.origins: A staple of 'Dealer's Choice' home poker games in the United States. It likely emerged in the mid-20th century as players sought to add more interaction to standard Seven-Card Stud.
timeline: 1950s: Becomes popular in American home-game circuits.
Present: A favorite in social poker clubs for its high pot-building potential.
history.cultural: Often the 'wildest' game in a poker night, known for generating massive pots due to the repeated betting and the slow-burn reveal of the rollout.
history.evolution: The game evolved from simple 'Pass the Trash' (one pass) into 'Anaconda' (three passes) to maximize the betting rounds and the 'trash' accumulation.

setup.players: Best with 6-8 players to ensure many cards are 'trashed'.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 7 cards face down. Initial ante or forced bets are placed.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best 5-card poker hand after three passing rounds and a 5-step rollout reveal.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Initial Deal**: 7 cards face down. 1st betting round. 2. **Round of 3**: Every player passes 3 cards from their hand to the player on their left. 2nd betting round. 3. **Round of 2**: Every player passes 2 cards to the player on their right. 3rd betting round. 4. **Round of 1**: Every player passes 1 card to the player on their left. 4th betting round. 5. **Selection**: Players choose their best 5 cards and discard the remaining 2 face down (these are dead). 6. **The Arrangement**: Players arrange their 5 chosen cards in a face-down pile in the order they wish to reveal them. 7. **The Rollout**: Each player reveals their first card simultaneously. Betting occurs. Then the second card, and so on, with betting after every reveal.
keyRules: No peaking: Once the 5 cards are stacked for the rollout, the order cannot be changed.
Full Pot: Because there are up to 8 betting rounds, Anaconda pots are significantly larger than standard poker pots.
High/Low Split: Common in home games, where the best high hand and best low hand (8-or-better) split the pot.

strategy.basic: Keep your 'core' cards. If you have a pair of Aces in your initial 7, never pass them, even if the other 5 cards are rubbish.
strategy.intermediate: The Trash Strategy: When passing, try to give your neighbor cards that don't 'connect'. If you have a 3, 5, and 9 of different suits, those are perfect 'trash' to pass.
strategy.advanced: Rollout Psychology: Order your reveal strategically. If you have 3-of-a-kind, revealing those three cards first can force opponents with weaker hands to fold before they even see your last two cards.
tips: The deck is exhausted quickly with 8 players. Pay attention to what YOU passed; those cards are likely still in play with your neighbor.
Don't be afraid to 'break' a weak flush draw to keep a strong pair of high cards, as the passing rounds make flushes harder to complete than you think.

variations.name: Anaconda 8-or-Better
variations.description: Pot is split between the high hand and the best low hand containing no card higher than an 8.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Hi-lo 8-or-better split for Anaconda is documented in rules text; specific low-hand and split-pot engine overrides are not modeled yet.

variations.name: Simple Pass the Trash
variations.description: Only one round of passing (usually 3 cards) before the discard and rollout.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Single-pass Pass the Trash adjusts only the passing pattern; engine progression and betting remain the same and are applied from the textual rules.

scoring.winCondition: High poker hand (or High/Low split) takes the pot.

synthesis.shortDescription: A high-interaction Poker variant featuring three chaotic passing rounds and a dramatic rollout reveal. Build your hand from the rubble of your neighbor's discards.
